body: This looks like a valid bug. Here is where it was fixed for full dates: https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/2aba8b0ff2c5d6979802b96842aceccad3d5716d

@pearlsze - I can no longer reproduce this. I can't see anything that has changed in the codebase to fix this. But then I wonder if there is something about the local timezone that makes the difference. Can you reproduce it with the latest Angular?

@petebacondarwin Hi, I made a new [stackblitz](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-v1ddqc?file=src/app/app.component.html) with the latest angular 11.1.1, and still see the issue.

The output I see (with the first one being incorrect). 
```
With YYYY-MM format
Input: 2019-02
Output: Jan. 2019

Specifying pipe to use 'GMT' timezone
Input: 2019-02
Output: Feb. 2019

With YYYY-MM-DD format
Input: 2019-02-01
Output: Feb. 2019

```

@pearlsze what timezone are you in? I am in London UK (GMT) and I don't see `Jan. 2019` I see `Feb. 2019`.
I tried overriding the timezone in Chrome but whatever time-zone I choose I get the same result.
@petebacondarwin I am in PST! Using the location override in Chrome (assuming you are too), "San Francisco" reproduces the issue, but for "London" I no longer see the issue.
Hmm, I tried "Mountain View"... let me try again.

OK!

In my local timezone `new Date('2019-02')` gives me `Fri Feb 01 2019 00:00:00 GMT+0000 (Greenwich Mean Time)`
And in San Francisco timezone `new Date('2019-02')` gives me `Thu Jan 31 2019 16:00:00 GMT-0800 (Pacific Standard Time)`
